summary: Siloam Springs lookout, Howell County, Mo.: work began Jan 1935, 99 ft 9 in tall; a 1963 survey note has it over a 1928 mark; listed as removed.

facts.agency: Mark Twain National Forest (per Forest Lookouts page header)
facts.status_note: Listed as removed on the Forest Lookouts page; no date or method given.

events.note: Work began in January 1935 at Highway 14 and Road T, for the Gardiner forestry unit, per the Willow Springs News item quoted on the page. Completion is not dated in the sources.
West Plains Journal item: planned circular drive, picnic tables and ovens, and a cabin for the tower guard.
Gasconade County Republican item says a fifth tower was being built near Siloam Springs. Not clear whether this is the same structure as the 1935 tower.
Albany Ledger item mentions picnic grounds located close to the tower.
Missouri State Highway Commission recovery note on the NGS mark: a forestry lookout had been built over the station mark.
Survey mark, not the tower, recovered in good condition by a Missouri Department of Natural Resources recovery note.
Listed as removed on the Forest Lookouts page; no date or method given.

notes_for_editor: Two sources. The 1935, 1936, 1937 and 1951 newspaper items are known only through the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes them; the originals were not checked. The brief's agency (Mark Twain National Forest) matches the page header, but the 1935 item names the Gardiner forestry unit as the builder, and ownership history was not verified. The 'second' tower in 1935 and 'fifth' tower in 1937 may refer to different structures; the story says so. The brief's coordinates match the NGS mark to within about 10 m. Removal is a bare 'Removed' label with no date or method. No access, visit or staffing beyond the 1936 guard-cabin plan was found. Web search found no tower-specific history.
